renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: orf_record
  title: ORF record
  description: |-
    The card shows every field of one RiboCode ORF: its gene, transcript, location, ORF type, length, P-sites in frame and adjusted periodicity p-value. It answers what is known about the ORF picked in the table.
    How to read: select a row in the table to fill the card. An ORF with many P-sites in frame 0 and a low adjusted p-value shows strong three-nucleotide periodicity, the signature of translation.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xryanglab/RiboCode/master/README.rst
  kind: record_card
  roles:
    id: orf_id
    title: gene_name

- component: card
  title: ORFs called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct ORFs RiboCode called as translated, and the ring splits them by class (annotated coding sequence, upstream, downstream, internal or novel ORF). It answers how much translation beyond annotated genes the data supports.
    How to read: most calls are usually annotated coding sequences. A large share of novel or upstream ORFs is the interesting part but needs follow-up, for example with a second caller.
  column: orf_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: orf_class
  caption: ORFs, by class

- component: card
  title: ORF length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ORF length in amino acids and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers whether the calls are full proteins or short ORFs.
    How to read: annotated coding sequences are long and small ORFs are short, so a histogram with a large short peak points to many upstream or novel ORFs. Filter by ORF class to separate them.
  column: aa_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: lengths, in amino acids

- component: card
  title: P-sites in frame
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of ribosome P-sites in the ORF's own reading frame and the histogram shows their distribution. It answers how much translation evidence each ORF has.
    How to read: ORFs with few in-frame P-sites rest on little signal even when their p-value passes. Treat low counts with caution and sort the table by this column.
  column: psites_frame0
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: P-sites in the ORF's own frame

- component: interactive
  title: ORF class
  description: Restricts every tile to the chosen ORF classes, such as upstream or novel ORFs. It answers
    whether a pattern belongs to annotated genes or to the new calls.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: orf_class

- component: table
  title: RiboCode ORFs
  description: |-
    Each row is an ORF in one library, with its gene, transcript, location, class, length, in-frame P-sites and adjusted periodicity p-value. It answers which ORFs to follow up.
    How to read: sort by the adjusted p-value or the P-site count and select a row to fill the ORF record.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: orf_id
